talks.title: Geometry, Symmetry, and Counting Curves: A Combinatorial Perspective
talks.speaker: Ryan Shifler
talks.abstract: Hilbert's 15th problem calls for a rigorous foundation for Schubert's calculus, which provides classical rules for counting geometric figures satisfying incidence conditions.

talks.title: Structure and dynamics of gene regulatory networks
talks.speaker: Claus Kadelka
talks.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) play a central role in cellular decision-making. Understanding their structure and how it impacts their dynamics constitutes a fundamental biological question.

talks.title: From harmonic analysis to exact signal recovery
talks.speaker: Alex Iosevich
talks.abstract: We are going to describe how classical techniques from harmonic analysis, such as linear and bilinear restriction theory, have been used to study signal recovery.

talks.title: Analysis of the adhesion model and reconstruction in cosmology
talks.speaker: Jian-Guo Liu
talks.abstract: In cosmology, a basic explanation of the observed concentration of mass in singular structures is provided by the Zeldovich approximation.

talks.title: Iterated Fourier Series
talks.speaker: Camil Muscalu
talks.abstract: The plan of the talk is to describe a bridge that connects in a natural way two mathematical worlds: the KdV equation and the absolute Galois group.

talks.title: Dilation Methods for Deterministic and Stochastic Dynamics with Quantum Computing Applications
talks.speaker: Xiantao Li
talks.abstract: Quantum algorithms are naturally formulated in terms of unitary dynamics, while many models from scientific computing involve dissipation, forcing, or randomness. In this talk I will describe a dilation-based approach for bridging this gap.

talks.title: Expander Graphs and Coding Theory
talks.speaker: Christine Kelley
talks.abstract: One fundamental goal in coding theory is to design explicit algebraic code ensembles that are asymptotically good.

talks.title: Real Time Bayesian Inference for Tsunami Early Warning
talks.speaker: Omar Ghattas
talks.affiliation: Oden Institute & Mechanical Engineering, UT Austin
talks.abstract: The Cascadia Subduction Zone (CSZ) extends over 1000 km from northern California to northern Vancouver Island, capable of unleashing a magnitude 9 earthquake with resulting 30 meter high tsunamis.

talks.title: Sublattices and Subrings of Z^n and Random Finite Abelian Groups
talks.speaker: Nathan Kaplan
talks.abstract: How many sublattices of Z^n have index at most X? If we choose such a lattice at random, what is the probability that the quotient is cyclic?

talks.title: Two Variations on a Theme by Cremona
talks.speaker: Aaron Bertram
talks.abstract: The Cremona transformation is a non-linear birational map between a projective space and its dual. It can be understood in terms of toric data.
